articles.title: NCPCR Probes Meta Over Child Exploitation Ads | Instagram Under Scanner | Big Tech Faces Heat
articles.description: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has launched a formal inquiry into Meta over allegations that advertisements linked to Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) appeared on its platforms. The inquiry follows a previous notice issued to the company after a BBC Eye investigation raised concerns about such advertisements. After reviewing Meta's response, the Commission has now escalated the matter into a formal fact-finding probe.The investigation is expected to examine the circumstances under which the alleged advertisements appeared, the effectiveness of Meta's content moderation systems, and whether existing safeguards were adequate to prevent the promotion of illegal content. articles.title: China Reveals Airborne Nuclear Strike System As Xi Flexes Strategic Firepower | WATCH
articles.description: China has publicly shown its airborne nuclear-strike system operating as a complete formation for the first time. Chinese military footage features an H-6N strategic bomber carrying a massive missile beneath its fuselage while two J-20 stealth fighters provide escort. China Daily identified the weapon as appearing to be the JL-1, a long-range air-launched ballistic missile believed capable of carrying conventional or nuclear payloads. The H-6N can be refuelled in flight, extending its operational reach, while the J-20s could protect the non-stealth bomber and help clear a launch corridor. The formation appeared in a simulated operation against a large enemy naval fleet. Beijing says its nuclear arsenal exists solely for deterrence and maintains a no-first-use policy. However, the public display sends a clear strategic message: China’s nuclear deterrent now visibly extends across land, sea and air. Watch.

articles.title: Pakistan's ISI, LeT Plot To Kill Sheikh Hasina, Ex-Bangladesh PM Ready To Defy Death, Arrest Threats
articles.description: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina says she is ready to return home despite the threat of arrest, prison or even death. But explosive reports citing intelligence sources now claim Pakistan's ISI, working through Lashkar-e-Taiba operatives, is plotting to assassinate her soon after she lands in Dhaka. The alleged plan reportedly involves suicide attackers, remote-controlled IEDs and even a car bomb disguised as a press vehicle. While these claims remain officially unverified, they come amid heightened security alerts and multiple recoveries of sophisticated explosive devices across Dhaka. In this video, we separate verified facts from unconfirmed allegations, examine why Hasina's return has become Bangladesh's biggest political and security test, and explain why India is watching every development closely. Could her return reshape Bangladesh's politics and India-Bangladesh ties? Watch this detailed analysis.
